focus: Session relaunch (v4.0.0.13 endless sessions, v4.0.0.14 opt-in per-runtime handover)
answeredQuestions: Session relaunch (v4.0.0.13, v4.0.0.14): do .skilled/hooks/session-relaunch and its runtime adapters implement the per-runtime SYSTEM_SESSION_RELAUNCH_<RUNTIME>_ENABLED flags, the 80 percent trigger and the model, effort and goal carry-over as the notes claim?

label: Effort carry-over exists for claude, codex and pi only: effort_is_valid() accepts those three names and append_effort_arguments() has a case arm for those three, so a proved sender effort on opencode, cursor or devin is dropped silently while v4.0.0.14:71 says the wrapper replays the launch effort in each runtime's own flag. Either those runtimes have no effort flag (note over-claims) or the wrapper under-implements; the pair is the defect.
confidence: high on code coverage, medium on which side is wrong

label: Outside the loop a prepare that omits --runtime is evaluated as claude: SKILLED_LOOP_RUNTIME defaults to 'claude' and the effective runtime is loopId ? envRuntime : (flagRuntime ?? envRuntime), so a pre-shell-line Pi or OpenCode session consults SYSTEM_SESSION_RELAUNCH_CLAUDE_ENABLED and writes a record typed runtime claude. The handoff doc phrases the omission rule only for --session, reading as if --runtime were neutral when it is a silent Claude default.
verify: SYSTEM_SESSION_RELAUNCH_ENABLED=1 SYSTEM_SESSION_RELAUNCH_CLAUDE_ENABLED=0 node .skilled/hooks/session-relaunch/bin/session-relaunch.cjs prepare --handoff <path> --session x  # refusal names the Claude switch

label: v4.0.0.14:55 still names HERMES among the seven per-runtime relaunch flags while v4.0.2.0 removed the runtime and dropped hermes from RUNTIMES in the same release; ENV-REFERENCE.md and both env examples list six with no hermes, and v4.0.0.1.md was amended in that diff window, so this note was simply missed.

dsh is absent from RUNTIMES, so runtimeEnableFlag('session-relaunch','dsh') is null, SYSTEM_SESSION_RELAUNCH_DSH_ENABLED resolves to nothing, and --runtime dsh throws before any note is read. Coherent with dsh shipping no relaunch adapter at all, so nothing is broken today, but v4.0.2.0:52's 'dsh sessions match Pi and OpenCode' is true for the advisor brief, goals and guards and false for the relaunch loop Pi and OpenCode also carry.
The wrapper never turns a proved sender model id into an argument before model_is_valid() bounds it to <=128 chars with no leading dash and no whitespace.
A carried effort is dropped when the model switched underneath it, because an effort chosen for one model can be rejected by another and the runtime default is the safe fallback.
SESSION_RELAUNCH_THRESHOLD is accepted only when finite in (0,1]; anything else, including an empty file read, falls back to 0.8 rather than to zero.
With SESSION_RELAUNCH_GOAL=0 neither prepare nor keep writes, replaces or removes the goal_packet field, so a note never holds a packet the switch said to drop.

The 80 percent trigger is real and single-sourced: DEFAULT_THRESHOLD=0.8 in lib/nudge.cjs, env-then-config resolution validated to (0,1], ratio measured by lib/context-usage.cjs against SESSION_RELAUNCH_WINDOW_TOKENS with autoCompactWindow then the model default. Release note and ENV-REFERENCE.md match the code.

Goal carry-over is implemented end to end at the note and wrapper layers: goal_packet rides the note, consume reports it, skilled-loop exports SESSION_RELAUNCH_GOAL_PACKET, a Codex sender is documented as unable to name a packet, and a manual claim follows the switch at claim time while a relaunch follows it as it stood when prepare wrote the record.

The relaunch adapter surface exists for four runtimes only (claude, codex, pi, opencode) while the flag surface covers six and the v4.0.0.14 note names seven. The mismatch is structural, not a single typo: flags, adapters and the note drifted apart across two releases.
Goal and model carry-over hold; effort carry-over does not hold for three of six runtimes, so the carry-over claim is only partly true.

direction: A defect in the 80 percent trigger or in its env override
reason: DEFAULT_THRESHOLD, the (0,1] validation and the ratio source all read as documented; the only oddity is the window resolution, which is described in ENV-REFERENCE.md:120 and matches the code's autoCompactWindow-then-model-default order.

direction: Hermes references surviving inside the session-relaunch hook tree
reason: grep -rn over .skilled/hooks/session-relaunch and .skilled/hooks/shared/hook-flags.cjs finds no hermes occurrence; the removal was complete in code and survives only in the v4.0.0.14 note text.

A reducer that ticks boxes from the state log alone cannot see this iteration answered its key question; the delta file is the only carrier of the full record.
